name: Lezer (@lezer/highlight)
description: CodeMirror 6's incremental LR parser system with a standalone highlighting API

host-language.comment: Written in TypeScript. Ships ESM and CJS builds with .d.ts typings, and is consumed from any JS runtime.

form-factor.comment: npm library only. There is no CLI.

license.comment: MIT. The official @lezer/* grammar packages are also MIT.

repository.comment: The project moved to Marijn Haverbeke's own Forgejo instance. The GitHub repo lezer-parser/highlight was archived on 2026-04-15 with a 'has moved' notice, and the npm manifest's repository field points to code.haverbeke.berlin.

documentation.comment: The highlight module section of the Lezer reference manual. The Lezer guide covers parsing, trees and mixed parsing, but not @lezer/highlight specifically.

first-release.comment: @lezer/highlight 0.16.0 was first published on npm on 2022-04-20, and 1.0.0 followed on 2022-06-06. Lezer itself was announced on 2019-09-03; before 2022 its highlighting lived in CodeMirror's @codemirror/highlight package.

engine-model.comment: A generated LR parser (@lezer/lr) produces a syntax tree. `styleTags` attaches highlight tags to node types, and `highlightTree` walks the tree.

regex-engine.comment: Tokens are declared in the grammar's @tokens block and compiled into the parser's tokenizer tables by @lezer/generator, plus optional hand-written external tokenizers. No regex engine runs grammars at highlight time.

embedded-languages.comment: Mixed-language trees are mounted with `parseMixed` / `NodeProp.mounted`, including overlays, and `highlightTree` descends into mounted and overlay trees, applying highlighters scoped to the inner language. Caveat: @lezer/highlight bundles no grammars, and @lezer/html nests JS and CSS only when the caller passes the @lezer/javascript and @lezer/css parsers to `configureNesting`, whose default is no nesting. CodeMirror's @codemirror/lang-html does this wiring for you. Rated true for consistency with the tree-sitter-highlight entry, where grammars are also supplied by the caller.

language-auto-detection.comment: No content-based detection; the caller picks the parser.

filename-extension-mapping.comment: Not in Lezer. The extension and filename to language table lives in CodeMirror's @codemirror/language-data, outside this candidate.

resumable-line-state.comment: No per-line state API. A parse can be advanced step by step (`startParse` / `advance`), and previous parses are reused through tree fragments, but there is no line-level state that can be saved and resumed TextMate-style.

incremental-reparsing.comment: Lezer's core design goal. Parses take cached tree fragments from the previous parse and reuse their nodes. `highlightTree` and `highlightCode` accept a from/to range, so you can re-highlight just the changed region of the new tree. Incremental reparsing lives in @lezer/common and @lezer/lr, which are required dependencies of the highlighter.

semantic-distinctions.comment: Tags come from syntax-tree context, e.g. in @lezer/javascript: `VariableDefinition` → definition(variableName), `CallExpression/VariableName` → function(variableName), `FunctionDeclaration/VariableDefinition` → function(definition(variableName)), `TypeDefinition` → definition(typeName). There is no scope-based locals resolution like tree-sitter's locals.scm.

bundled-languages.comment: @lezer/highlight is engine-only; its sole dependency is @lezer/common. Languages come as separate grammar packages. The Lezer site lists 16 (C++, CSS, Clojure, HTML, Java, JavaScript, Julia, JSON, Lezer, Markdown, PHP, Python, Rust, Sass, XML, YAML), checked 2026-11-18; more are community-maintained.

grammar-format.comment: `.grammar` files are compiled by @lezer/generator. Highlighting is attached with `styleTags` in JS code. @lezer/markdown is a hand-written parser that produces Lezer trees.

grammar-ecosystem-compatibility.comment: Consumes only Lezer trees. CodeMirror's @codemirror/legacy-modes (stream parsers) are a CodeMirror feature, not part of Lezer.

runtime-grammar-loading.comment: Highlighting rules can be added or changed at runtime through `parser.configure({props: [styleTags({...})]})` or `NodeSet.extend`. A whole grammar can be compiled in memory with @lezer/generator's `buildParser`, though the docs say this is 'mostly useful for testing'; the normal workflow compiles grammars at build time.

lazy-grammar-loading.comment: Nothing is bundled up front, and each grammar is its own npm package, so apps import only what they need (e.g. via dynamic import). Lezer itself has no on-demand loader; CodeMirror's language-data adds async loading.

grammar-accuracy.comment: No bundled grammars, and no systematic accuracy evidence found for the official @lezer/* grammars. Not rated.

bundled-themes.comment: No themes or stylesheets ship; the 1.2.5 tarball contains only dist JS and typings. `classHighlighter` is a tag-to-class mapping (`tok-*` classes) for styling with external CSS, not a theme. Themes such as One Dark are CodeMirror packages.

theme-format.comment: A highlighter is defined in JS with `tagHighlighter([{tag, class}])` or a custom `Highlighter.style(tags)`. Visual styling then lives in user CSS, e.g. against `classHighlighter`'s stable `tok-*` classes.

token-classification.comment: Uses `tags.*` (comment, keyword, variableName, typeName, ...) with parent fallback (`Tag.define(parent)`) and modifiers (definition, function, constant, local, special, standard).

css-class-output.comment: Highlighters return space-separated class strings; `classHighlighter` emits stable `tok-*` classes for external CSS.

multi-theme-output.comment: `highlightTree` accepts an array of highlighters and combines their classes in one pass, but no light/dark mechanism is documented and no stylesheets ship.

public-token-api.comment: `highlightTree(tree, highlighter, putStyle(from, to, classes), from?, to?)` and `highlightCode(code, tree, highlighter, putText(text, classes), putBreak(), from?, to?)` are documented exports. Callbacks are the only output channel.

ir-kinds.comment: token-list: callback streams of (from, to, classes) or (text, classes) plus line breaks. syntax-tree: the full Lezer `Tree` with typed nodes (SyntaxNode, TreeCursor) is the input and is fully documented; `getStyleTags(node)` exposes per-node tags.

serializable-ir.comment: Callback output and in-memory Tree objects only; there is no documented JSON or hast serialization.

theme-resolved-tokens.comment: Highlighters produce class strings, not colours or styles. CodeMirror's HighlightStyle generates CSS rules, which is still class-based.

source-offsets-in-ir.comment: `highlightTree`'s `putStyle` receives from/to character offsets, and tree nodes carry from/to positions.

custom-formatter-api.comment: Rendering is entirely up to the caller through the `putStyle` / `putText` / `putBreak` callbacks, and a custom `Highlighter` (style + scope) can be implemented.

line-transforms-decorations.comment: No line or range annotation mechanism. Decorations are a CodeMirror editor feature.

output-formats.comment: No first-party formatter. Even `highlightCode` only calls putText/putBreak callbacks, and the caller builds the HTML, DOM or anything else.

line-numbers.comment: No rendering, so no line numbers. `highlightCode` signals line breaks through `putBreak`.

streaming-output.comment: Highlighting needs a finished Tree. Parses can be advanced in steps and stopped early, but no documented API emits highlighted output before the input is fully parsed.

native-dependencies.comment: Pure JS; its only dependency is @lezer/common.

runs-in-browser.comment: Pure ESM JS, and powers in-browser highlighting in CodeMirror 6.

synchronous-api.comment: `highlightTree` and `highlightCode` are synchronous, and so is `parser.parse(code)`. No async initialisation.

bindings-ports.comment: No official or well-known bindings or ports in other languages were found. Not exhaustively verified.

core-package-size.comment: Bundlephobia min+gzip for @lezer/highlight 1.2.5 (27,073 B minified), checked 2026-11-18. Bundlephobia counts the bundled @lezer/common dependency. Excludes @lezer/lr and any grammar package, which are needed to actually highlight code.

throughput-tier.comment: No independent comparative benchmark against other highlighters found.

initialization-cost.comment: Unmeasured. Grammars are precompiled parse tables loaded as JS modules, so startup is probably light, but no measurement was found.

github-stars.comment: The canonical repo is now on code.haverbeke.berlin (Forgejo), not GitHub. The archived GitHub mirror lezer-parser/highlight has 41 stars as of 2026-11-18, which understates popularity.

monthly-downloads.comment: npm downloads for 2026-10-18 to 2026-11-16, checked 2026-11-18. Mostly transitive installs through CodeMirror 6.

maintenance-status.comment: Releases on 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-28 fall within 6 months. The API is stable and changes rarely, mostly bug fixes. Development moved from GitHub to code.haverbeke.berlin in April 2026; the GitHub repo is archived, but the project is not.

documentation-quality.comment: A dedicated docs site with a system guide, a thorough reference manual and examples. Standalone highlighting has no guide chapter (it is reference-only), and there is no theme catalog.

notable-users.value: CodeMirror 6 (@codemirror/language); JupyterLab (@jupyterlab/codemirror); the official @lezer/* grammar packages (e.g. @lezer/html)
notable-users.comment: Traced through direct npm dependencies on @lezer/highlight. Every CodeMirror 6 embedder depends on it transitively.

bus-factor.comment: Marijn Haverbeke is the sole npm maintainer and the primary author.
